question: Vancouver Mayoral Election Winner
resolution_criteria:
The 2026 Vancouver mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 17, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Vancouver as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Vancouver.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
# Vancouver mayoral election 2026: research as of 2026-10-06

### 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on a consensus of credible reporting. If results are ambiguous, official City of Vancouver results decide it. No URL is given in the criteria.
- Advance voting runs on Oct 3, 7, 10 and 13. [Daily Hive](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/how-to-vote-vancouver-municipal-civic-elections-october-2026-locations-identification-eligibility)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The real contest is between Pete Fry (Green) and incumbent Ken Sim (ABC Vancouver).
- Several listed options are not running for mayor:
  - **William Azaroff (OneCity)** withdrew on 2026-09-08 and endorsed Fry.
  - **John Coupar** is running for council with the Vancouver Liberals, not for mayor.
  - **Tim Louis** appeared only in 2025 hypothetical polls and is not a declared candidate.
- Declared mayoral candidates: Sim, Fry, Kareem Allam (Vancouver Liberals), Rebecca Bligh (Vote Vancouver), Colleen Hardwick (TEAM), Muhammad Ahmad, and independents Amauri Caliman and Scott Gilbert. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Vancouver_municipal_election)
- Hardwick is a real candidate who is not on the option list, so she falls under "Other".

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-10-05: there was a televised mayoral debate. Separately, Sim skipped at least one debate (UBC Robson Square) and turned down Fry's challenge to a one-on-one debate. [Global News](https://globalnews.ca/news/12103468/vancouver-mayoral-debate/), [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/ken-sim-skips-first-vancouver-mayoral-debate/), [Castanet](https://www.castanetkamloops.net/edition/news-story-634293-99-.htm)
- 2026-09-16: Justason poll (fielded Aug 31 to Sep 11, 336 decided voters, online). Decided voters: Fry 45%, Sim 30%, Hardwick 11%, Allam 10%, Bligh 5%.
  - During fieldwork, Fry rose from 38% to 59% and Sim fell from 33% to 24%. The post-Sep 8 figures rest on only 119 interviews, so they are less reliable.
  - Women: Fry 60%, Sim 19%. Men: Sim 39%, Fry 32%.
  - [Justason](https://www.justasonmi.com/?p=6484)
- 2026-09-08: Azaroff (OneCity) withdrew and endorsed Fry. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Vancouver_municipal_election)
- 2026-09-02: Stephanie Allen (COPE) withdrew and endorsed Fry. This left Fry as the only candidate from COPE, OneCity and the Greens. [Justason](https://www.justasonmi.com/?p=6484)
- 2026-08-04: Research Co. poll (fielded Jul 30 to Aug 1). Decided voters: Sim 30%, Fry 19%, Allam 19%, Hardwick 14%, Bligh 7%, Azaroff 5%, Allen 4%. [Research Co.](https://researchco.ca/2026/08/04/vanpoli-2/), [BIV](https://www.biv.com/news/commentary/mario-canseco-sim-leads-vancouver-mayoral-race-but-field-remains-wide-open-poll-says-12625842)
- Jul 20 to 24: Pallas Data poll, including undecideds: Fry 18.1%, Sim 13.8%, Allam 11.5%, Hardwick 10.5%, undecided 33.8%. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Vancouver_municipal_election)
- A Leger poll was fielded Sep 23 to 30, but it was published after Oct 6, so I left it out.

### 4. Base rates
- 2022: Sim beat incumbent Kennedy Stewart with about 51% of the vote. Stewart served one term.
- Gregor Robertson was re-elected in 2011 and 2014.
- Overall, Vancouver incumbents running again have a mixed record: one recent defeat and two re-elections.
- Undecided shares in 2026 polls are high, at roughly 26% to 34%.
- Consolidation of the progressive vote behind one candidate has historically mattered under first-past-the-post. Research Co. noted that about a third of the vote could be enough to win. [Research Co.](https://researchco.ca/2026/08/04/vanpoli-2/)
- Vancouver civic polling is sparse and mostly online panels. The two late-summer polls disagreed sharply: Sim led by 11 in one, and Fry led by 15 in the other.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket: the "Vancouver Mayoral Election Winner" market opened 2026-04-02, with about $179K in volume. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/vancouver-mayoral-election-winner)
- 2026-07-31: Fry reached about 26%. [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/pete-fry-reaches-26-to-win-2026-vancouver-mayor-jul-31-2026)
- 2026-08-05: Sim was at about 30%. [PredictionHunt](https://prediction.com/news/ken-sim-hits-30-to-win-vancouver-mayor-despite-aug-05-2026)
- 2026-08-21: Fry was at about 29%. [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/vancouver-mayor-polls-pete-fry-odds-29-aug-21-2026)
- 2026-09-08: Sim was at about 50%. [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/cope-withdrawal-backfires-ken-sim-hits-50-sep-08-2026)
- Mid to late September: after Azaroff's endorsement, Fry reportedly jumped about 32 points. Sim reportedly fell from 52% to 34% on Kalshi and Polymarket, his first time priced as the underdog. Allam fell 11 points around Sep 22. These figures come from aggregator summaries, so I could not confirm exact dates. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxvancouvermayor/who-will-win-the-vancouver-mayoral-election/kxvancouvermayor-26oct17)
- About 2026-10-06: one Polymarket snapshot showed Fry 68.1% and Sim 30%. Allam and Coupar were under 1%. This comes from an aggregator snapshot, so treat it as approximate. [polym.trade](https://polym.trade/event/vancouver-mayoral-election-winner)
- A UBC economist warned that these markets are thin and reflect "vibes" more than reliable information. [Iredell Free News](https://www.iredellfreenews.com/gaming/2026/prediction-markets-enter-bc-mayoral-races-but-experts-say-dont-trust-the-odds/)
- I found no expert or model-based forecasts.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More advance voting days: Oct 7, 10 and 13.
- More polls are likely: Leger, a Canada Pulse Insights poll for OMNI, and possibly Research Co.
- More debates are expected, along with possible further endorsements or consolidation, for example among Allam, Bligh and Hardwick voters.
- 2026-10-17: general voting day. Unofficial results are expected the same night, and official certification follows a few days later.

- 2026-09-16: Justason poll of decided voters had Fry 45%, Sim 30%, with Fry's lead widening late in fieldwork. The sample was small.
- 2026-08-04: Research Co. had Sim ahead (30 to 19). That was before consolidation, so it is outdated.
- Early October: Sim skipped at least one debate and declined a one-on-one with Fry. This suggests a defensive or trailing campaign.
- About 2026-10-06: Polymarket showed Fry about 68% and Sim about 30%. The market is thin, but it matches the post-consolidation polling.

Where I moved and why:
- The incumbency base rate alone would favour Sim at about 55 to 60%.
- The consolidation and the latest poll push Fry clearly ahead.
- I anchor close to the market, shading Fry slightly down to about 64%. Polling is sparse and contradictory, undecideds are high, and Sim's base (ABC money and turnout operation, plus men voting for him) could narrow the gap.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:**
- The centre-right vote quietly consolidates. Allam and Hardwick voters drift to Sim as the only viable non-progressive.
- Turnout favours ABC's organised base.
- Sim wins narrowly, with Fry's online-panel lead having been overstated.

A far less likely path is a late Hardwick or Allam surge in a fragmented race, where about 33% could win.
